SFLOW-V5-4.3-1.note: Unconditional MUST of the sFlowAgentAddress DESCRIPTION (4.3), binding the sFlow agent Ze is. parseAgentAddress checks only that the configured agent-address parses and is specified; no Go code in the tree implements an SNMP agent (grep: snmp appears only in ifIndex/ifTable comments), so nothing answers SNMP at the address. {gap} annotation and Meta Support coverage disclose it.

SFLOW-V5-4.3-2.note: SHOULD: on a multi-homed agent the address should be the loopback address. validateSFlowCollectors checks a specified address, equal on every sflow collector, and nothing checks it belongs to a loopback interface; only docs/guide/flow-export.md recommends one. {gap} annotation and Meta Support coverage disclose it.

SFLOW-V5-x-1.note: single-polarity: the header's first field decodes big-endian to 5, the only datagram_version the XDR union defines; WriteDatagramHeader writes a constant, so any other value fails the assertion

SFLOW-V5-x-10.note: Single-polarity row. TestSFlowV5SamplingRateIsTheSourceRate drives the real EncodeFlowSample with two sources at 74565 and 1000 and requires each datagram's sampling_rate to equal its source's rate, so a constant, a stale rate or a literal goes red (recorded). sampling_worker.go fills FlowSample.Rate from the psample packet's rate.

SFLOW-V5-x-11.note: asserts the code's estimate sample_pool = min(seq*rate, MaxUint32), not the RFC's 'Total number of packets that could have been sampled'; no packet count the data source saw is observed, and the saturation subtest asserts behaviour the RFC does not state (an XDR unsigned counter wraps; a saturated pool stops advancing)

SFLOW-V5-x-12.note: positive: ifIndex 0x01000000 and 0xFFFFFFFF decode unchanged from expanded counter format 4 and flow format 3; negative: indexes at and above 2^24 never alias to their low 24 bits in source_id_index or if_counters.ifIndex

SFLOW-V5-x-14.note: notifySnapshot now polls at elapsed >= interval - one snapshot tick and waits for the mutex instead of TryLock-dropping. TestSFlowV5CounterGapNeverExceedsInterval drives 30 late 1.01 s snapshots at a 5 s interval through a real Sender and requires no gap over 5 s and at least 6 polls; the old elapsed >= interval gate leaves a 5.05 s gap and goes red (author observed red at HEAD). Its two tags sit on one assertion: the maximum is one upper bound, so this is effectively single-polarity, not a pair. TestSFlowCounterPollAtInterval covers the 1 s interval. The busy-exporter drop is covered under x-26.

SFLOW-V5-x-15.note: single-polarity (marker: interfaceCountersFrom has no differencing path): a second conversion of the same kernel stats must equal the first, so a delta implementation (which loses the traffic of a lost sample) fails 'second conversion differs'; the negligible-wrap clause rests on 64-bit octet counters, and RxBytes 5e9 > 2^32 must come through untruncated

SFLOW-V5-x-16.note: Integer clause: TestSFlowV5UnknownEgressInterfaceIsZero requires output format 0 and value 0 for an unknown egress. Counter clause: TestSFlowV5UnavailableCountersCarrySentinelEveryPoll requires exactly 0xFFFFFFFF for the four counters the kernel does not expose, and TestSFlowV5AvailableCountersNeverTurnUnavailable requires real values (including zero) for the rest. All three units now carry observed-red records.
SFLOW-V5-x-16.upgrade_reason: The earlier weak verdict rested only on the counter-clause units lacking a discrimination record; both now carry observed-red records against interfaceCountersFrom. Re-read both units: they assert the exact sentinel and the exact available values, so a 0-for-unknown or sentinel-everywhere producer fails.

SFLOW-V5-x-2.note: Row narrowed to its last two sentences (invariance, unique key); SNMP and loopback moved to gap rows SFLOW-V5-4.3-1/4.3-2. Invariance: TestSFlowV5AgentAddressIsTheAgentKey drives the factory-built counter encoder over three interface sets and requires 192.0.2.1 in every header; TestSFlowDatagramHeaderIPv4 pins the header bytes. No code path derives the address from interfaces, so invariance has no reject path (positive only). Unique key: Config.Validate refuses a missing, 0.0.0.0, :: or second agent address, naming agent-address (parseAgentAddress, differentAgents); TestSFlowV5AgentAddressSpellingsNameOneAgent accepts two spellings of 2001:db8::1 and refuses ::1 vs ::2, which fails if the compare returns to strings (D-8 fixed). All units recorded (revert).

SFLOW-V5-x-25.note: positive: one sample yields exactly one datagram sent at once; negative: three samples yield three datagrams, the sender count advancing by one each, and no datagram carries more than one flow_sample

SFLOW-V5-x-26.note: Chain now whole. TestSFlowV5DueCountersAreSent requires every due poll over 30 late ticks to send a datagram listing all three interfaces, and requires a due snapshot that meets a held exporter mutex still to send them (the old TryLock drop goes red). The real encoder's part: writeCounterDatagrams units require all 30 sources emitted with the partial tail not held back, and TestSFlowV5ConfiguredMaxDatagramBoundsEveryDatagram counts all 30 samples on the collector socket through CounterEncoder.Encode. Trigger (x-14) now enforced.

SFLOW-V5-x-27.note: Ze cannot promise its ifIndex stays below 2^24 (Linux ifindex is a full int), so it falls in the quote's 'Otherwise' branch and the compact-for-all clause does not bind it; mixing: a compact format 1 or 2 among the six records fails 'compact data_format emitted'; expanded for all: alternating low and full-width ifIndex values fail 'want expanded 4' and 'want expanded 3' if any interface drops to compact

SFLOW-V5-x-28.note: Per-source clause: TestSFlowV5FlowSequencePerSourceID interleaves sources 3 and 4 and requires 1,2,3 and 1,2, so one sequence shared across source_ids goes red (recorded). Reset clause: TestSFlowV5PoolAndSequenceResetTogether and TestSFlowV5PoolNeverResetsWithoutSequence (both recorded).

SFLOW-V5-x-29.note: Reset clause: TestSFlowV5SequenceResetOnAnyCounterGoingBack rewinds each of 13 cumulative counters and requires sequence 1; TestSFlowV5SequenceResetWithCounters requires source 3's reset on ifInOctets going back. Increment and no-spurious-reset: TestSFlowV5SequenceNeverResetWithoutDiscontinuity requires 1,2,3 while counters rise. All units now recorded.
SFLOW-V5-x-29.upgrade_reason: The earlier weak verdict rested only on TestSFlowV5SequenceNeverResetWithoutDiscontinuity and TestSFlowV5SequenceResetWithCounters lacking discrimination records; both now carry observed-red records against resetSequencesOnDiscontinuity. Re-read: they assert exact sequence values, so a never-reset or always-reset producer fails.

SFLOW-V5-x-3.note: single-polarity: agent_address and sub_agent_id 7 both decode to the distinct values written, so the pair the header carries names the sub-agent's datagram stream

SFLOW-V5-x-30.note: positive: a CounterGeneration change with rising counters resets the sequence to 1; negative: an unchanged generation keeps 1,2,3 even when a counter reads lower

SFLOW-V5-x-31.note: Only-one-sub-agent: TestSFlowV5OneSubAgentPerDataSource requires Config.Validate to accept two sflow collectors with sub-agent-id 7 and to refuse 7 and 8, naming sub-agent-id (validateSFlowCollectors; every sflow collector exports every data source); TestSFlowV5DataSourceKeepsOneSubAgent shows one collector's counter and flow factories use its single sub-agent. Constant-association: the sflow_v5_test.go negative keeps ifIndex 3 on one sub-agent over five datagrams. All units recorded.

SFLOW-V5-x-32.note: positive: every counter unavailable on the first poll is still the sentinel on a poll with different statistics; negative: available counters stay available on a later zero-valued poll

SFLOW-V5-x-33.note: positive: the flow_sample carries one sampled_header record with the 14 captured bytes; negative: a 1500-byte capture that cannot fit is truncated but still carried as a non-empty sampled_header prefix

SFLOW-V5-x-34.note: positive: a 60-octet skb gives frame_length 64 and stripped 4, the FCS added to both; negative: over 64, 1500 and 9000 octets frame_length minus stripped is always the skb length

SFLOW-V5-x-4.note: single-polarity (marker: the exporter holds no path that emits a datagram without advancing): writeCounterDatagrams' two datagrams carry sequence 1 and 2 and return 3 as the next, so a sender that did not increment per datagram fails seq2 != 2 and nextSeq != 3

SFLOW-V5-x-5.note: Single-polarity row. TestSFlowV5ConfiguredMaxDatagramBoundsEveryDatagram sets a non-default 600-octet bound on a real Sender, requires every counter datagram for 30 interfaces to be <= 600 octets while together carrying all 30 samples (num_samples summed on the collector socket), requires a flow sample with a 1400-octet header to arrive in <= 600 octets, and requires Sender.Send to refuse 601 octets; the older default-bound unit TestSFlowMultiInterface stays. An encoder bounding by the default instead of the configured size goes red.

SFLOW-V5-x-6.note: Single-polarity row. TestSFlowV5FlowSampleSentWithinOneSecond hands a sample to the real sflow FlowEncoder with a real Sender and requires the datagram on the collector socket within one second of the call, so an encoder holding a sample longer than 1 s goes red while one flushing sooner passes, matching the quote; TestExportFlowSampleDispatch proves exportFlowSample dispatches synchronously. Counter samples are sent synchronously in the poll (x-26 units).

SFLOW-V5-x-7.note: Single-polarity row, every sflow writer now compared as XDR words with distinct-octet values: datagram header and sampled_header padding (TestSFlowV5FlowDatagramIsXDR), counters_sample wrapper (TestSFlowV5CounterSampleWrapperIsXDR), all flow_sample words (TestSFlowV5FlowSampleWordsAreXDR), extended_gateway IPv4 and IPv6 unions and variable-length arrays (TestSFlowV5ExtendedGatewayIsXDR), if_counters (TestSFlowIfCounters). A little-endian, reordered or unpadded write changes compared bytes. Every unit recorded.

SFLOW-V5-x-9.note: positive: counter and flow datagrams of one sender share one datagram sequence that wraps through 0xFFFFFFFF; negative: a counter generation reset restarts only the source sample sequence, never the datagram sequence
